column3: NASB supplies “me” after “has commanded”; the Hebrew has no object there.
“your son and your grandson” renders “your child and your child’s child.”
“has promised” renders “spoke”; NASB supplies “in” before “a land.”
“The LORD is our God, the LORD is one” is one reading of four Hebrew words, “Yahweh our God Yahweh one”; the meaning can also be “the LORD our God, the LORD is one.”
“teach them diligently” renders a verb meaning “repeat” or “sharpen.”
“frontals on your forehead” renders “marks between your eyes.”
“wipe you off the face of the earth” renders “destroy you from on the face of the ground.”
“in time to come” renders “tomorrow”; NASB supplies “mean.”
“always” renders “all the days”; “for our survival” renders “to keep us alive.”
“if we are careful” renders “that we are careful.”
